MEASURED 2026-08-26 by reading the `hxm_program` working tree, then CORRECTED TWICE by its owner within minutes. Both corrections are kept, because the sequence is the useful part: an inference was drawn from a file listing, published, and then dismantled by two facts nobody could read off the tree.

🛑 **CORRECTION 1 — "NO COMMITTED EXPORT" WAS FALSE.** `reflow2.json` sits at the repo ROOT, not under `docs/design/` where reflow2's own convention puts it and the only place checked. **Absence measured by looking in one conventional location is not absence.** Third instance of that class today: `unallocated_component` reported 33 "empty" parts that were real modules; the three-legs audit v1 matched case-sensitively and reported a present detector as missing.

🛑 **CORRECTION 2 — THE HEADLINE INFERENCE IS DEAD.** Anthony, asked directly: **"I built hxm_program before I built reflow2, so much of it was hand-rolled prior to me adopting reflow2 on it."** The parallel tooling is **INHERITANCE, NOT A WORKAROUND**. It is not evidence of a reflow2 gap, and this node's original claim — that a user "built parallel graph tooling because reflow2 does not do this" — asserted a motive that never existed. **The tools predate the tool they were supposedly working around.**

⭐ **AND THAT IS WHY THE CAVEAT WAS THERE.** The first version listed three things the finding did not establish, and #2 was *"it does not date the tooling — any of it may predate the adoption, making it inheritance rather than workaround. Nothing here distinguishes those, and the difference decides whether this is a gap or a habit."* **The caveat named the exact question, one question answered it, and the answer killed the inference.** Cost: one sentence. Had the caveat been left off — or had the finding been reported as a gap — the design would now hold a false claim about a user's motives, and somebody might have built against it.

═══ WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE OF THE TREE ═══

  `reflow2.json`  a COMMITTED EXPORT at the repo root — 259 nodes, 501 edges,
                  stamp 0.40.0, written 2026-08-26 20:28. 71 Decision, 29
                  Artifact, 28 Capability, 27 Requirement, 20 DesignRule, 19
                  ChangeEvent, 17 Question, 12 Verification, 11 Component, 11
                  Fragment, 6 Interface, 3 Contributor. Real and actively kept.

  `codegraphs/` (per-repo: hex, hex-acq-pyepics, hextools, nslsii),
  `docs-graph/`, `dataflow/`, `DECISIONS.md` (338 lines) — **all predating the
  reflow2 adoption.** A program that existed first and had reflow2 adopted ONTO
  it, which is `adopt`'s whole premise rather than a complaint about it.

═══ WHAT REMAINS WORTH ASKING, NOW THAT THE WRONG QUESTION IS CLOSED ═══

The interesting fact is no longer *why did they build it* but **what happened after adoption**: reflow2 and the inherited tooling now COEXIST, and nobody has asked which parts reflow2 displaced, which it duplicates, and which it has never reached. `DECISIONS.md` at 338 lines beside 71 Decision nodes is the sharpest instance — migration, rendering, or two records drifting apart are three different situations and the tree cannot tell them apart.

⚠️ **AND THE GENERAL LESSON, WHICH IS ABOUT ADOPT AND NOT ABOUT THIS PROGRAM:** every brownfield adoption inherits tooling, and reflow2 has no way to ask *what did this project already have, and what should now retire*. `adopt` brings a system under design control and says nothing about the instruments the project was already using. Whether that is a gap or correctly out of scope is untested, and this node is not evidence either way — it is one program, and the owner wrote both halves.
